races.title: State Senate, District 2
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Damon Connolly
cands.bio: Attorney and Democratic politician. Worked as an associate at Thelen LLP, then as a California deputy attorney general and supervising deputy attorney general (1993-2007), and was a partner at Girard Gibbs LLP. San Rafael City Council 2007-2014, Marin County Board of Supervisors 2015-2022, and California Assembly (District 12) since December 2022.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists his 2026 endorsements as including the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, Working Families Party, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

cands.gaps: The pages we had did not give his birthplace or when he came to California, only that he was raised in the Bay Area. They did not show any specific bill he sponsored, speech or action on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, police funding, guns, abortion, or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so no stated positions came from that source. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or stated stances on data centers or development in the pages provided.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says he was raised in the San Francisco Bay Area and earned degrees at UC Berkeley and UC Berkeley School of Law; it gives no birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney who worked at a law firm, spent about 14 years at the California Department of Justice (deputy and then supervising deputy attorney general), and was a partner at a law firm. Held local office on the San Rafael City Council (2007-2014) and Marin County Board of Supervisors (2015-2022), then served in the State Assembly from December 2022.
qual.why: Prior state legislative service and a long law and government legal career fit the job of writing law and the state budget, and he also has local elected experience.

cands.name: Tief Gibbs
cands.bio: Novato business owner and co-owner of Vintage Vehicles, with an economics degree from San Diego State University (1995). Secretary of the Marin Republican Central Committee and past president of Novato Republican Women. Ran for U.S. House in District 2 in 2024 and for State Senate District 2 in 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: California Rifle and Pistol Association, according to her campaign site.
Reform California, plus several voter-guide groups (Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn), per Ballotpedia's 2026 listing.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was raised or when, if ever, she moved within California. She has no voting record, since she has never held office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from her on data centers, housing or land development, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, or property tax relief for homeowners; she speaks only in general terms about lower taxes and reduced spending. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or specific pledges on donor money. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so her 2026 positions come from her campaign site and her 2023 survey and 2024 website.

local.label: Roots 55: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Palo Alto, and she graduated from San Diego State University in 1995 and has run a business in Novato; her upbringing and any move are not documented, so the score rests on 30 years of adult residence in California.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Co-owns Vintage Vehicles in downtown Novato with her husband, holds an economics degree, and serves on the Novato Downtown Business Association board. She has held no elected or legislative office.
qual.why: Business ownership and an economics degree place her in the middle range; there is no legislative, budget or policy career, and board and party-committee roles add nothing to the score.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she strongly supports Second Amendment rights and is endorsed by the California Rifle and Pistol Association.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site says immigration enforcement is crucial to her and calls for secure borders and cooperation with federal law enforcement on immigration laws.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she places significant emphasis on pro-life policies.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she stands behind tough-on-crime policies and supports law enforcement agencies.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her 2024 campaign website said she supports school choice and vouchers and gives parents greater control over their children's education. It did not mention teacher pay.
